title: A shape with Heesch number 7
credit: Heesch (1968); Bašić (2021); posed as a target by Epoch AI FrontierMath open problems
premise_risks: Already a public FrontierMath target, so it is curated rather than new
Corona conventions: hole-free vs holes-allowed outer corona (H_h ∈ {H_c, H_c+1}); fix hole-free
No shape with H=7 may exist; then the problem is a (hard) impossibility question
plain: Some shapes cannot tile the whole plane but can still be surrounded by a ring of copies of themselves, and that ring by another ring, and so on, up to some limit. The number of rings possible is the shape's Heesch number. The record is 6, found in 2021. Find a shape whose Heesch number is finite but at least 7.
math: For a closed topological disk $T\subset\mathbb R^2$ that does not tile the plane, the Heesch number $H(T)$ is the largest $k$ such that there is a patch of congruent copies of $T$ made of $T$ surrounded by $k$ successive coronas. Each corona is a ring of copies covering a neighbourhood of the previous patch's boundary, and each intermediate union must be a closed disk (no holes). Exhibit $T$ with $7\le H(T)<\infty$. Polyform version: exhibit a polyomino, polyhex or polyiamond with $7\le H<\infty$.
review_note: Known: Record $H=6$ (B. Bašić, 2021). Kaplan's SAT method ('Heesch numbers of unmarked polyforms', arXiv:2105.09438, Contrib. Discrete Math. 17 (2022)) computed Heesch numbers exhaustively for polyforms up to 19-ominoes, 17-hexes and 24-iamonds and found nothing above the record. In $\mathbb E^3$, finite Heesch numbers are unbounded (arXiv:2610.24281, Oct 2026), which says nothing about the plane. Listed as unsolved by Epoch AI FrontierMath (hole-free $H_c$ convention, with a 200-cell polyform witness format).
